key_findings.finding: The available evidence does not establish that ADAM10 is the sole or dominant LRP1 sheddase in brain endothelium. The focal study itself states that multiple proteases contribute to LRP1 ectodomain shedding. Searches specifically combining LRP1 shedding with MT1-MMP/MMP14 and BBB/Aβ did not identify a direct competing BBB study; the retrieved MT1-MMP paper concerned LDLR ectodomain shedding, not LRP1 or Aβ BBB efflux. Therefore, ADAM10-specific attribution is supported by pharmacologic and endothelial-genetic concordance, but comparative separation from MT1-MMP/MMP14 is incomplete.

source_tools.relevance: Study abstract explicitly notes multiple proteases contribute to LRP1 shedding
Targeted MT1-MMP/MMP14-LRP1-BBB search yielded no direct study and retrieved only an LDLR-shedding paper
Review confirms LRP1 shedding is one of several regulators of vascular Aβ clearance but does not provide ADAM10-vs-MMP14 causal comparison

key_findings.finding: No human interventional or observational evidence directly linking ADAM10 inhibition/activity to endothelial LRP1 ectodomain shedding, membrane LRP1 abundance/function, and Aβ trans-BBB efflux was identified in the searches. The evidence base is therefore cellular and murine, with no demonstrated clinical translation.

Focused ADAM10 inhibition/Aβ transcytosis/LRP1 search did not retrieve additional direct studies

entities.name: PMID:27503326
observations: 2016 study reports that GI254023X blocked Aβ42-induced extracellular LRP1 increase and increased fluorescein-Aβ transcytosis in HBMEC BBB cultures.

Endothelial-specific ADAM10 knockout mice had lower brain LRP1 shedding and enhanced BBB Aβ clearance; in an AD mouse model, GI254023X lowered shedding and increased plasma Aβ40, while brain Aβ reductions were not significant.
Study supports ADAM10 as a contributor, not necessarily the sole LRP1 sheddase; direct human clinical evidence was not identified.

entities.name: ADAM10
observations: Inhibition or endothelial deletion reduced LRP1 shedding and increased Aβ BBB transport/clearance in experimental systems, chiefly one 2016 study.

entities.name: LRP1
observations: Ectodomain shedding is reduced by ADAM10 inhibition in experimental brain endothelial systems; improved Aβ transcytosis/clearance is consistent with preserved functional LRP1, though increased surface abundance was not directly established.

source_tools.relevance: Shedding and BBB efflux findings; mechanistic caveat.

entities.name: ADAM10 LRP1 BBB
observations: In HBMEC cultures, Aβ42 approximately doubled extracellular LRP1; GI254023X abolished this increase and raised fluorescein-Aβ transcytosis dose-dependently, with significant effects above 1 μM and increases of at least about 1.25-fold.

Endothelial ADAM10 knockout reduced LRP1 shedding and enhanced BBB Aβ clearance in mice; inhibitor-treated AD-model mice showed increased plasma Aβ40, but brain Aβ reductions were not statistically significant.

source_tools.relevance: Quantitative cellular and in vivo results from the focal study.
